evidence_grades.vendor_published: Directly stated by a primary vendor source.
evidence_grades.literature_derived: Derived from a public design or paper; not a measured HBF product specification.
evidence_grades.exploratory_assumption: Chosen to close an unpublished specification or expose a sensitivity axis.
evidence_grades.implementation_policy: Defines simulator or composition behavior rather than a hardware fact.

allowed_overlaps.hbf-page-size: The 4 KiB page is both part of the assumed 512 GiB mixed-radix geometry and independently bounded by the related XL-FLASH public page size; both records are needed and their notes distinguish the claims.
allowed_overlaps.hbf-hbio-bw: The vendor-published 1600 GB/s baseline and the separately derived 8388.608 GB/s cost-unbounded array-supply upper bound intentionally share one config key; their records distinguish the evidence grades and profile scopes.

hbm_address_mapping.notes: Derived bursts interleave across stack/channel/pseudo-channel, then bank group/bank/column/row; reversible high-bit swizzles spread common power-of-two strides across pseudo-channels and banks. This is an optimistic controller mapping policy, not a JEDEC fact. The scheme id is emitted in every summary so results remain auditable if mapping policy changes.

hbf_placement_mapping.notes: Consecutive logical data pages are striped one per HBF stack. A deterministic 64-bit rotation changes lane ownership per stack-local mapping group so power-of-two tensor/KV strides do not pin a phase to one stack. Every stack's full L2P table is resident in its controller DRAM; dirty 512-entry groups persist as stack-local checkpoint pages. EC5 static-direct reuses the identical data-page stack owner and per-stack round-robin plane order, but omits resident-FTL lookup/update and checkpoint work. The mapping is emitted in every summary and is a simulator policy, not a published HBF address map.

parameters.notes: The vendor's decimal 1.6 TB/s is 1600 GB/s. HBFSim treats that aggregate target as decoded external payload per stack. For a 4096 B + 224 B codeword, the vendor-anchored use-case profiles provision four raw 421.875 GB/s channels and sixteen raw 105.46875 GB/s ECC lanes. The shared TSV is 1712.5 GB/s because the model serializes both each 4320 B codeword and one 64 B internal command there. Those interface names, topology, OOB/command uplifts, and per-resource allocations are modeling assumptions, not independently published hardware facts. This record does not support the separate cost-unbounded output-upper-bound profile.

parameters.profile_value: 8388.608 GB/s per stack only in usecase-baseline-output-upper-bound.cfg
parameters.notes: This cost-unbounded sensitivity matches HBIO to the modeled decoded array supply: 64 planes/stack x 32 subarrays/plane x 4096 B / 1000 ns = 8388.608 GB/s. It is an arithmetic upper bound for the assumed topology, not a vendor bandwidth claim or a cost-neutral design.

parameters.profile_value: 512 GiB computed capacity per stack
parameters.notes: The shipped mixed-radix geometry computes 512 GiB, about 7.4% above 512 GB. Only die count and die density are vendor-published; the channel/plane/block/page decomposition is assumed. Capacity-ratio profiles derive blocks-per-plane from this same assumed geometry rather than adding an independent hardware fact.
XL-FLASH is a related low-latency SLC technology, not a public HBF product measurement.

parameters.profile_value: 1000 in every usecase-*.cfg experiment profile
parameters.source_value: 1 us NAND-cell read; 0.29 us modeled on-chip transfer; 1.29 us total page read
parameters.notes: All EC topology points use the same paper-derived 1 us cell-read value so stack count is the only hardware-axis change. With the common 250 ns modeled response and explicit command/transfer stages, HBFSim produces 1283.77 ns for one uncontended 4 KiB read. The 4 us point remains available only as an explicit sensitivity.

parameters.profile_value: 95000 in every usecase-*.cfg experiment profile
parameters.notes: HBFSim exposes a separate 5000 ns verify phase, so every EC topology point uses 95000 ns program plus 5000 ns verify to reproduce the paper's assumed 100 us cell-write latency. Other program times remain explicit sensitivities, not topology-dependent defaults.
Exposed independently so program and verify uncertainty can be swept.

parameters.profile_value: 250 in every usecase-*.cfg experiment profile
parameters.notes: The paper reports only a 0.29 us aggregate on-chip read latency, not an ECC-only value. Every EC topology point uses 250 ns as a common calibration residual: together with HBFSim's explicit command and transfer stages it yields a 1283.77 ns uncontended page read, close to the paper's 1.29 us. This is not a measured ECC latency. HBFSim requires the response latency to cover the raw-codeword initiation interval.

parameters.profile_value: 105.46875 GB/s per die for vendor-anchored 16-die use-case profiles; 552.96 GB/s per die for the cost-unbounded output upper bound; 135 GB/s per die for 8-die server profiles
parameters.notes: The vendor publishes only aggregate 1.6 TB/s read bandwidth, not ECC topology or throughput. Values provision each profile's assumed die count so aggregate payload throughput, after 4096 B + 224 B codeword overhead, matches its modeled HBIO read target. The 552.96 GB/s upper-bound value is derived from 8847.36 raw GB/s divided over sixteen assumed die issue ports. These are compatibility bounds, not ECC measurements.

parameters.profile_value: equal to decode raw bandwidth in each profile, including 552.96 GB/s per die in the cost-unbounded output upper bound
parameters.notes: No public HBF write-side ECC throughput is available. Equal encode/decode provisioning is a symmetric baseline assumption; NAND program timing normally dominates writes and the parameter must be swept for write-path studies.
No public HBF source currently supports the exact value.

parameters.profile_value: see resolved scenario config
parameters.notes: Public HBF material does not provide enough internal topology or per-stage bandwidth detail to calibrate these independently. Channel, media-lane, and page-buffer values are raw page+OOB rates in HBFSim; the shared TSV carries both raw codewords and internal commands; HBIO and logic SRAM use decoded payload rates. The local-output profile changes only lanes and banks from 16 to 32 for one output per modeled subarray. The cost-unbounded upper bound retains existing resource counts but provisions four channels at 2211.84 raw GB/s each, 8388.608 decoded GB/s logic SRAM/HBIO, an 8978.432 GB/s shared TSV for each 4320 B codeword plus its 64 B command, a 7.8125 ns per-die flash-TSU interval, and a 0.48828125 ns logic-dispatch interval. These values match the assumed 8388.608 GB/s decoded array supply rather than a published product.
The exact batch scheduler and round-join rules are not specified by the fact sheet; independent-subarray mode is an optimistic sensitivity bound.

parameters.profile_value: use-case profiles: 2048 GB/s read, 512 GB/s write, 0 ns added fixed latency; server profiles: see resolved config
parameters.notes: The TCAD design supplies the use-case 2048/512 GB/s bandwidth point but does not state a separate fixed D2D latency, so the paper-oriented profiles add 0 ns. Sandisk's public fact sheet states 1.6 TB/s first-generation HBF stack read bandwidth, but it does not publish a separate HBM-to-HBF/HBF-to-HBM D2D bandwidth or latency; 1.6 TB/s must not be relabeled as a D2D measurement. Server profiles are independent exploratory sensitivities. This is not a vendor-measured HBF interface.

parameters.profile_value: use-case profiles: 48 GiB/stack at 2/4/6/8 stacks; server profiles: 32 GiB/stack at 4 stacks
parameters.notes: Both the 48 GiB use-case point and 32 GiB server point are simulator capacity assumptions, not declarations of shipping products. Micron's current public HBM4 page reports 36 GB for a 12-high stack; capacity and stack-count sensitivity must remain explicit.

parameters.profile_value: use-case: 32 x 64-bit channels and two 32-bit pseudo-channels/channel; server: 16 x 64-bit channels and two 32-bit pseudo-channels/channel
parameters.notes: Synopsys publishes the HBM4 limit of 32 channels/64 pseudo-channels, and Micron publishes a 2048-pin interface; 64-bit channel and 32-bit pseudo-channel widths follow arithmetically for the use-case profile. The server profile deliberately halves the channel count to a 1024-bit sensitivity point and is not claimed as the same HBM4 product topology.
Cadence reports BL8 for HBM4. Combined with each pseudo-channel width, HBFSim derives burst bytes rather than configuring them independently.

parameters.profile_value: use-case HBM4-width profile: 16 bank groups x 4 banks = 64 banks per pseudo-channel
parameters.notes: Synopsys publishes 64 banks per pseudo-channel for its HBM4/4E controller. The use-case 16-by-4 decomposition is the simulator's explicit mapping choice. The server 4-by-4 geometry is also an explicit exploratory assumption, not a sourced product claim.

parameters.profile_value: 6.4 Gb/s/pin in normalized use-case profiles; 8.0 Gb/s/pin in server profiles
parameters.source_value: 8 Gb/s/pin and about 2 TB/s for a 2048-bit HBM4 interface
parameters.notes: The server rate uses the source's 8.0 Gb/s reference point on a deliberately reduced 1024-bit topology. The 6.4 Gb/s use-case point is an unsourced normalization that yields 1638.4 GB/s on 2048 bits for comparison with 1.6 TB/s HBF. Neither combined simulator profile is a shipping-product declaration; Micron's current HBM4 page separately reports more than 11 Gb/s and more than 2.8 TB/s.

parameters.profile_value: 4 data transfers per command clock; tCCD_S/L = 2/4 command-clock cycles
parameters.notes: Micron's published patent application gives a related-art HBM example at 8 Gb/s, BL8, a 2 GHz command clock, and tCCD_S/L of 2/4 clocks so 32-byte pseudo-channel bursts fill the DQ bus. HBFSim preserves those dimensionless ratios at the normalized 6.4 Gb/s sensitivity point; this is a source-anchored extrapolation, not a normative HBM4 speed-bin table.
The model divides this evenly across pseudo-channels, giving 1 KiB per pseudo-channel when two pseudo-channels are enabled. HBM4 product pages do not publish a complete row mapping for this profile.

parameters.profile_value: 0 ns address-map delay; 14/14 ns tRCD, 14 ns read latency, 10 ns write latency, and the fully resolved values in each config
parameters.notes: No public HBM4 vendor speed-bin table supports this complete timing set. HBFSim treats these as minimum physical delays and rounds every command issue to the derived command-clock grid. They must be swept or replaced by a pinned vendor/standard profile before absolute product claims.

parameters.profile_value: see resolved scenario config
parameters.notes: Controller DRAM defaults to the exact full-resident page-level L2P footprint and is partitioned evenly per stack. Mapping accesses reserve a short pipelined issue slot and then observe an overlappable response latency; neither value is a published HBF limit. Capacity, metadata, buffering, and controller-credit assumptions must be swept and coupled to an area/power model before physical design claims. The page-read queue depth is per stack and bounds page children after a memory-object request is split.

parameters.profile_value: see resolved scenario config
parameters.notes: FTL maintenance policy and reserve settings. They control when and how the modeled controller performs GC; they are not published HBF media parameters and require workload sensitivity sweeps.

parameters.profile_value: coalescing enabled; acknowledgement before flush
parameters.notes: Controller acknowledgement and volatile coalescing semantics. Experiments must report these choices because they change burst latency and the separation between user completion and drain makespan.

parameters.profile_value: On-package LPDDR: 2 TiB, 16 assumed media channels, 512 global credits, 2/20 ns assumed controller issue/process, 100 ns media latency, 2000/2000 GB/s aggregate media and dedicated M2S/S2M, zero propagation; CXL memory: 256 GiB, 8 media channels, 512 global credits, 2/20 ns controller issue/process, 90 ns media latency, 204.8 GB/s aggregate media, 36/36 GB/s M2S/S2M, 75 ns one-way propagation; NVMe SSD: 4 TiB, 4 media channels, 512 global credits, 20/500 ns controller issue/process, 80/100 us media latency, 14/7 GB/s aggregate media, 16/16 GB/s M2S/S2M, 250 ns one-way propagation; all use 4 KiB pages and 64/16 B command/completion records
parameters.notes: HotInfra Table 1 anchors only the on-package LPDDR 2 TiB, 2 TB/s nominal read bandwidth, and 100 ns point. Its write bandwidth, controller/link decomposition, channel count, credits, and protocol records remain assumptions. The CXL/NVMe specifications anchor direction and request/completion semantics; the Micron and KIOXIA pages anchor only product-class capacity and throughput envelopes. Exact controller intervals, media channels, global credits, fixed latencies, protocol-record sizes, and several bandwidth values remain explicit exploratory assumptions. These profiles are reproducible no-HBF sensitivity points, not calibrated LPDDR, CPU-memory, CXL, PCIe, or SSD product models. Every field must be reported and swept before absolute claims.

parameters.profile_value: see resolved scenario config
parameters.notes: Composition policy knobs; report them as evaluated mechanisms, not hardware facts. layer-buffer-bytes is the upper bound for one EC6 layer buffer. Runtime sizes both parity buffers to the actual maximum per-layer model/KV data footprint; only scratch and metadata remain permanently HBM-resident, and the configured maximum is not statically reserved.
